name: Spark plug
summary: A small part that makes the spark that lights the fuel and air in a petrol engine.
whatItDoes: Each cylinder of a petrol engine has a spark plug. It fires at exactly the right moment in every cycle to start combustion. Diesel engines don't use spark plugs: they light their fuel by squeezing the air until it is hot enough.
howItWorks: An ignition coil builds up a very high voltage and sends it to the plug. The voltage jumps a small gap between the plug's two electrodes inside the cylinder and makes a spark. The engine computer (ECU) times the spark based on engine speed and load.
failureSymptoms: Rough idle or the engine shaking
Misfires, often with a flashing check-engine light
safetyNotes: Let the engine cool fully first. Aluminium cylinder heads strip threads easily when hot.
Ignition systems make very high voltage. Switch the ignition off and unplug the coils before working.
